chunks: By this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ayman ibn Muhriz, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no servant from our Shia who rises to pray except that angels surround him, equal in number to those who oppose him, praying behind him and supplicating to God on his behalf until he completes his prayer.

key_terms.اكتنفته: Surrounded/enveloped him — denoting protective encirclement by angels
key_terms.شيعتنا: Our Shia — the followers and partisans of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.ملائكة: Angels — celestial beings who worship God and serve His creation

ai.seo_question: Do angels pray behind a Shia Muslim during prayer according to hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) informed Abu Hamza al-Thumali that when a Shia believer stands for prayer, angels gather around that worshiper in a number matching all those who oppose him, joining in prayer behind him and making supplications on his behalf until the prayer concludes. This hadith was narrated in the 85th assembly of al-Amali by Shaykh al-Saduq in Rajab 368 AH, encouraging the Shia community in their devotion by assuring them of divine angelic support during worship.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from Ayman b. Mahraz from Muhammad b. al-Fadl from Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Abi Ja`far (as).

He said: There is not a worshiper from our Shi`a except that when he rises to pray, there is an angel for every person that opposes him praying behind him and supplicating to Allah on his behalf until he completes his prayer.
